question: After catastrophic forgetting and loss of plasticity are controlled, does sequentially observing disjoint data chunks still produce worse representations than training on the same data jointly, and which continual-learning mechanisms recover that missing benefit?

key_findings.claim: The authors identify a residual 'co-observation' deficit: retaining every sequential checkpoint does not match incremental joint training, even when four chunks are random i.i.d. partitions rather than different tasks.
key_findings.evidence: At chunk 4, linear-probe accuracy for capacity-controlled ensemble versus incremental joint was 70.25% versus 74.29% on supervised CIFAR-100, 80.57% versus 82.75% on supervised ImageNet-100, 71.53% versus 73.50% for Barlow Twins on ImageNet-100, and 58.83% versus 62.64% for I-JEPA on ImageNet-100. Results are means over 3 seeds, except the main I-JEPA baselines use 6 seeds.

key_findings.claim: Replay improves representation quality through more than retention: sufficiently large buffers exceed the perfect-retention ensemble and move toward incremental joint training.
key_findings.evidence: With 12,500 exemplars per past chunk, roughly 30% of each chunk, chunk-4 accuracy was 81.27% versus 80.55% for the unreduced ensemble and 82.75% for incremental joint in supervised ImageNet-100; 72.59% versus 71.25% and 73.50% for Barlow Twins; and 60.21% versus 59.82% and 62.64% for I-JEPA. The fixed iteration budget rules out extra optimization steps as the explanation.

key_findings.claim: Representation distillation behaves mainly as a retention mechanism in these experiments and does not recover the full joint-training advantage.
key_findings.evidence: At chunk 4, LwF reached 79.93% versus 80.55% for the ensemble and 82.75% for incremental joint in supervised ImageNet-100; CaSSLe reached 72.07% versus 71.25% for the ensemble and 73.50% for incremental joint with Barlow Twins. Ensembles built from distillation-enhanced checkpoints remained below incremental joint training.

key_findings.claim: The ensemble is a credible zero-forgetting diagnostic but not a literal ideal continual learner.
key_findings.evidence: Per-chunk training accuracy never declined after a chunk was learned, while replacing naive checkpoints with LwF or CaSSLe checkpoints yielded only marginal or no improvement. The authors nevertheless note that concatenated frozen states cannot reproduce seamless parameter-level forward and backward transfer.

method.core_idea: Separate representation loss caused by missing simultaneous data access from forgetting and plasticity by comparing four controlled training regimes and evaluating only frozen backbones.
method.mechanism: A naive sequential learner exposes both forgetting and missing co-observation. An ensemble concatenates all historical backbone states to preserve learned features; optional PCA returns its representation to one-backbone dimension. Incremental joint training repeatedly trains on all data seen so far, supplying co-observation while sharing the repeated-optimization plasticity burden. A global linear probe trained after each stage removes classifier-head drift. The ensemble-to-incremental-joint gap is treated as evidence for the representational value of co-observation, then replay and distillation are located relative to these baselines.
assumptions: Concatenating all frozen checkpoints, with PCA when needed, is an adequate proxy for perfect feature retention.
A global linear probe measures representation generality without materially favoring one training regime.
Fixed iteration counts make comparisons of data-access patterns fair even though individual methods may have different optimal schedules.
After the retention and transfer ablations, the residual ensemble-to-incremental-joint gap is primarily caused by missing co-observation rather than another sequential-optimization confound.

techniques.role: Freezes every stage's backbone and concatenates their features so information available at any earlier stage remains accessible to a single downstream readout.
Compresses the ensemble feature vector back to the dimension of one backbone, reducing the chance that raw dimensionality explains its performance.
Freezes the backbone and fits a fresh classifier on all accumulated data, isolating representational generalization from continual classifier drift.
Randomly partitions one dataset into sequential i.i.d. chunks to study fragmented access without a macroscopic task or class shift.
Mixes stored past exemplars with current data in each minibatch, approximating the cumulative joint distribution during optimization.
Builds ensembles from LwF or CaSSLe checkpoints to test whether weak forward or backward transfer, rather than absent co-observation, explains the residual gap.

evaluations.setting: Four i.i.d. chunks of CIFAR-100, supervised ResNet-18, fixed per-chunk iteration budget equivalent to 100 offline epochs, 3 seeds.
evaluations.metric: Chunk-4 top-1 linear-probe accuracy, mean plus or minus standard error.

evaluations.setting: Four i.i.d. chunks of ImageNet-100, supervised ResNet-18, fixed budget equivalent to 90 offline epochs, 3 seeds.
evaluations.metric: Chunk-4 top-1 linear-probe accuracy, mean plus or minus standard error.
evaluations.baseline: Offline joint training reached 83.68±0.11%; the unreduced ensemble reached 80.55±0.10%.

evaluations.setting: Four i.i.d. chunks of ImageNet-100, self-supervised Barlow Twins with ResNet-18, 400-equivalent epochs per chunk, 3 seeds.
evaluations.metric: Chunk-4 top-1 linear-probe accuracy, mean plus or minus standard error.
evaluations.result: Naive 69.25±0.06%; ensemble PCA 71.53±0.31%; incremental joint 73.50±0.41%; 30% replay 72.59±0.09%; CaSSLe 72.07±0.23%.
evaluations.baseline: Offline joint training reached 76.42±0.40%; the unreduced ensemble reached 71.25±0.19%.

evaluations.setting: Four i.i.d. chunks of ImageNet-100, self-supervised I-JEPA with ViT-B/16, 400-equivalent epochs per chunk; 6 seeds for primary baselines and 3 for replay.
evaluations.metric: Chunk-4 top-1 linear-probe accuracy, mean plus or minus standard error.
evaluations.result: Naive 53.83±0.60%; ensemble PCA 58.83±0.69%; incremental joint 62.64±0.55%; 30% replay 60.21±0.99%.
evaluations.baseline: Offline joint training reached 69.35±0.38%; the unreduced ensemble reached 59.82±0.46%.

limitations: Author-stated: the ensemble expands representation capacity and PCA is only a post-hoc approximation to a parameter-matched ideal learner.
Author-stated: identical schedules prioritize controlled comparison rather than each method's best achievable accuracy.
Author-stated: experiments cover moderate-scale vision models; billion-parameter overparameterization may change the effect.

Reviewer inference: a linear probe can recover distributed information that an online nonlinear decision process might not access, so the diagnostic does not measure every practical form of usability.

Reviewer inference: calling the residual gap co-observation is supported by several controls but is not a causal intervention on data simultaneity alone; trajectory length, revisit frequency, and sample mixing remain coupled.
failure_modes: The diagnostic loses validity if PCA discards task-relevant low-variance directions differently across methods.
Replay may fail to exceed retention when the buffer is too small or unrepresentative to create useful cross-partition minibatches.
Distillation cannot reconstruct shared features absent from the teacher's representation, so it can preserve an incomplete basis indefinitely.
The co-observation gap may shrink when a frozen pretrained backbone already contains the cross-domain features that sequential training would otherwise need to discover.
Privacy, storage, or compute constraints may prevent replay or cumulative joint training even when their representational advantage is known.
reusable_insights: Evaluate continual learners against a perfect-retention proxy, not only naive and joint endpoints, to avoid labeling every residual deficit as forgetting.
Treat minibatch composition as an optimization control variable: which examples are visible together can determine which shared features become identifiable.
A distillation method can be successful at retention while still failing at cross-distribution synthesis; report those capabilities separately.
Use i.i.d. chunking as a hard negative control for claims that continual-learning failures require explicit distribution shift.
For memory selection, optimize not only coverage of old data but also the cross-example interactions the buffer creates with current data.
open_questions: Can synthetic feature replay or sufficient statistics restore cross-partition constraints without storing raw examples?
Which batch-level interaction measures predict the minimum replay buffer needed to exceed perfect retention?
Does the co-observation gap persist at billion-parameter language-model scale after controlling for pretrained feature reuse?
Can an online objective explicitly reward features that remain useful across latent partitions before those partitions are jointly visible?
How much of the residual gap is attributable to within-minibatch co-occurrence versus repeated interleaving over a longer optimization horizon?

competitive_landscape.title: Chunking: Continual Learning is not just about Distribution Shift
competitive_landscape.difference: Lee and Storkey establish that i.i.d. chunking itself causes a large continual-learning deficit and attribute much of it to forgetting; this paper adds a full-retention ensemble to isolate a remaining deficit attributed to missing simultaneous observation.

competitive_landscape.title: Knowledge Accumulation in Continually Learned Representations and the Issue of Feature Forgetting
competitive_landscape.difference: Hess et al. use representation evaluation to show that feature forgetting impedes knowledge accumulation; this paper repurposes checkpoint ensembles and linear probes to hold forgetting fixed and study what retention cannot recover.

competitive_landscape.title: Where is the Truth? The Risk of Getting Confounded in a Continual World
competitive_landscape.difference: Busch et al. construct temporally varying spurious correlations that joint training can ignore but sequential training cannot; this paper argues that the same missing cross-partition constraints create a generic deficit even under random i.i.d. partitions without engineered confounders.

competitive_landscape.title: Revisiting Catastrophic Forgetting in Class Incremental Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Ni et al. identify inter-phase confusion in class-incremental learning and propose a contrastive correction; this paper generalizes the concern beyond class boundaries and frames it as a representation deficit caused by separate data access.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper presents co-observation as a third facet of continual learning, distinct from forgetting and loss of plasticity, and argues that replay restores cross-partition optimization constraints rather than merely preserving old outputs.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper combines i.i.d. chunking, full-retention checkpoint ensembles, capacity matching, global linear probes, transfer-enhanced ensemble ablations, and supervised and self-supervised experiments; the cited prior work studies chunking, feature forgetting, inter-phase confusion, or constructed confounders separately.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The phenomenon is not wholly new because prior chunking and confounder papers expose closely related deficits. The main contribution is a sharper isolation protocol and unifying interpretation. Confidence is moderate-high, not definitive, because the ensemble is still an approximation to an ideal single continual learner.

reviewer_notes: Author claim: the ensemble-to-incremental-joint gap is primarily a co-observation effect. Reviewer inference: the controls make that interpretation plausible but do not eliminate every optimization-path confound. Quantitative values were checked against Appendix F page markers, not read from plots. Competitive-landscape metadata was checked against primary arXiv abstract pages.
